title: Credit surface gap causing multi-tenant outages
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description: Several customers reported sustained 429s and opaque errors across Hosted and Dedicated during a traffic surge after a routine rollout. Root cause surfaced as a mismatch between the token/credit fingerprinting used by the orchestrator and the edge admission proxy after a minor hash change in the runtime. The change caused credits to be attributed to ephemeral ledger keys that the proxy did not recognize, resulting in wholesale credit denial for affected tenants (warmup and burst paths). Private clusters with older runtime exhibited a different failure mode (silent admission with degraded SLOs).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy runtime-1.22.0 -> runtime-1.22.1 to a two-region test cluster with sticky credit caching enabled
2) Simulate short high-QPS burst from a tenant that expects burst credits (use loadgen script with tenant token and warmup pattern),
3) Observe orchestrator ledger incrementing credits under new fingerprint key while proxy admission queries old key -> proxy denies admission and returns 429
4) Reproduce locally by toggling CREDIT_FINGERPRINT_VERSION env var between 'v1' and 'v2' in orchestrator and proxy to force mismatch
timeline_and_comments: 2025-02-12 08:13 UTC - Pager alert: surge of 429s for multiple enterprise tenants. SRE on-call (Ethan) paged in. Initial hypothesis: quota reconciliation lag.
2025-02-12 09:02 UTC - Discovered correlation between deploy to runtime-1.22.1 and increased opaque 429s. Confirmed spike across both hosted and dedicated pools. Opened emergency channel #inc-991234.
2025-02-12 10:15 UTC - Hotfix step 1: increased emergency burst quota for affected tenants to reduce immediate customer impact (manual override). Reduced 429 rate by ~60% for some tenants.

2025-02-12 12:00 UTC - Instrumented additional tracing at admission boundary and orchestrator ledger reads. Found mismatched cache keys: orchestrator wrote to 'credit_v2:<tenant>:epoch' while proxy queried 'credit_v1:<tenant>:epoch'.

2025-02-12 14:30 UTC - Root cause confirmed: hash fingerprinting change in runtime-1.22.1 refactor. Regression slipped past unit tests because integration test for credit fingerprint compatibility was missing.

2025-02-12 16:40 UTC - Emergency patch authored: PR #8123 adds backward-compatible fingerprint translation layer in proxy and an orchestrator reconciliation endpoint. Deployed canary to 2 hosts in us-west-2.
2025-02-12 18:10 UTC - Canary metrics: 95th latency unaffected, 429s reduced to baseline on canary. Rolled patch to remaining hosts in region. Continuing Dedicated rollouts.

2025-02-13 03:20 UTC - Private customer clusters: manual coordinator contacted. Provided migration script and backfill instructions; one private cluster required operator-assisted ledger replay (scheduled maintenance window).
2025-03-01 11:05 UTC - Postmortem investigation started. Assigned follow-ups: add integration test matrix, build reconciliation job, improve deploy gating for fingerprint-affecting changes.
2025-03-04 09:00 UTC - Patch merged and included in runtime-1.22.1.ETA for full fleet rollover: 2025-03-12. Ticket remains In Progress to track follow-ups and audits.
mitigation_taken: Increased emergency burst allowances for impacted tenants to reduce immediate 429s
Canary deployment of proxy translation layer to convert v2->v1 fingerprints on admission path
Temporary admission bypass for warmup traffic for validated enterprise tenants (manual ACL list)
Provided ledger replay/backfill tooling to private customers and scheduled operator window
root_cause_summary: A refactor changed the fingerprinting/hash scheme used to derive per-tenant credit ledger keys. The change was deployed to orchestrator and proxy at slightly different times and without a compatibility shim. This produced a window where orchestrator writes used the new keyspace while proxies continued to read the old one, causing admission failures. Missing integration tests and deploy gating for fingerprint-affecting changes allowed the regression through.
fix_description: Implemented a translation shim in the proxy that understands both v1 and v2 fingerprint keys and will consult the orchestrator reconciliation endpoint when cache misses occur. Added orchestrator endpoint to surface alternate key mappings and to backfill short-lived epochs. Added automated integration tests that exercise mixed-version clusters and included a deploy-gate in CI that blocks rolling when fingerprint-affecting files change without a compatibility shim.
rollback_plan: If the translation shim causes regressions, we will revert runtime-1.22.1 to runtime-1.22.0 in the affected pools using the standard rollback playbook. Before revert, we will disable the shard-level sticky cache to avoid lingering mismatched entries. SRE to coordinate with on-call and customers for scheduled reverts in Dedicated/private where necessary.
postmortem_and_followups: Create an integration test suite that simulates mixed fingerprint versions (owner: Ethan) - estimate 5 pts
Implement periodic reconciliation job that detects and repairs ledger key divergence (owner: Priya Shah) - estimate 8 pts
Add telemetry alerts for sudden increase in credit cache miss ratio (owner: Observability) - estimate 3 pts
Update deploy gating to require compatibility shim or migration plan if fingerprinting code is touched (owner: CI) - estimate 2 pts
Run customer-facing postmortems and credit adjustments for impacted tenants (owner: CS Ops)
